subject: Stuart Broad has revealed his greatest Test XI featuring only players he faced during his international career
posts:
Broad's XI sparks debate by omitting the highest run-scorer in Test history. A subjective list masquerading as an objective peak.
Evidence: Personal preference, Statistical omission, Historical record
#Cricket #StuartBroad

Stuart Broad claims his Test XI represents the best players he faced during his career, focusing on balance and impact across different eras of the game.
Stated Judgement: (1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

The reality is a subjective selection that excludes Sachin Tendulkar, the statistically greatest run-scorer in Test history, highlighting personal bias over objective metrics.
Resulting Judgement: (0.0, 0.0) — Neutral

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Stasis.
The selection is a personal opinion piece, not a factual claim, making the omission a matter of taste rather than a structural failure.
Stuart Broad, a retired England fast bowler, compiled an all-time Test XI from opponents he played against. The list includes legends like Muralitharan and Kallis but notably omits Sachin Tendulkar.

The Bright Side:
It highlights the immense depth of talent Broad faced, showcasing the global reach of Test cricket legends.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is a confusion of WHO (the selector) with WHAT (the objective best). It is a subjective list presented as a definitive XI.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic exercise in personal branding. By creating a controversial list, Broad generates engagement through the 'snub' of a legend, leveraging fan loyalty to keep his name in the news cycle.

The Trajectory: The Path of Stasis.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Stasis. The subjective nature of the list ensures no objective harm is done.

The Unavoidable Truth: Broad faced many legends.

The Unavoidable Lie: This list is an objective ranking of the best players.

Alethekanon:
An audit of the selection reveals a reliance on personal experience over aggregate data. It is a narrative construct, not a statistical analysis.

Awwthekanon:
It is okay to have favorites! Even legends have their own heroes and rivals they respect most.

Brothekanon:
Broad just wanted to stir the pot. Leaving out Sachin is basically a guaranteed way to get the internet talking.
